lines.direction: Deliver it as an understated three-word cold open. Speak in one brisk breath, perfectly clear. A little stress on finance, with a definite ending and no pause in the middle. Around 1.1 seconds.

One brisk deadpan sentence, exactly three words. Land the word accounting clearly as the profession, pronounced uh-KOWN-ting. Give the word a little space after killed. No added article, no extra words. Around 1.15 seconds.
Third item in a deadpan list. The same brisk three-beat cadence. Keep video editing connected, finish on editing with a tiny smile. Around 1.4 seconds.
A dry, incredulous understatement directly to camera. Lean a little on ONE. Speak conversationally in about 1.4 seconds.

lines.text: Okay. That one was kind of cool.
lines.direction: A tiny smile she cannot hide. A short beat after Okay, then the rest in one breath. Wry and slightly smug on cool. Aim for 1.8 seconds.
A small conspiratorial invitation, as though she is showing a friend a trick. Soft and expectant, under a second.

Speak precisely three words: Claude, killed, programmers. Use the same dry, matter-of-fact list cadence. Leave a very short silent beat after the D of killed, then start the P of programmers directly. Pronounce only the supplied three words. No articles. Finish the boast crisply in about 1.25 seconds.
Lower her volume like she is asking someone standing next to her for a discreet favor. Small pause after Alex, then an awkward casual question. Around 1.3 seconds.
Completely deadpan, quiet and precise. Three words as one short statement, with a clean downward landing on right. Around 1.25 seconds, no sigh, laugh, or trailing sound.
